title: Rule Record (Rules Registry)
description:
Every rule has a named owner, a source, a disposition into an enforcing control, and a review-by date. This is the regdelta pattern: external change -> named owner -> disposition -> executable control.

**G7's two halves, and what each word means here.**

*No immortal rules*: `review_by` is required, and so is `source.effective`. Until M09 `effective` was optional and the review-by assertion in `tests/test_contracts.py` was guarded `if effective:`, so a rule that simply omitted the field was never examined -- ADR-053 planted `effective` deleted, `status: enforced`, `review_by: "2099-01-01"` and measured 2079 passed on a literally immortal enforced rule. Requiring the field closes that door and leaves the other one ADR-053 named OPEN: the review-by assertion still exempts `status: enforced`, so an enforced rule may still carry a distant `review_by`. Bounding that needs a horizon Legal/S&P chooses, and it is recorded as open rather than reported as done (ADR-075 amendment 2).

*No orphan rules* means ONE thing, and this sentence is the definition: **an orphan rule is a rule whose disposition names an enforcing control -- any `controls[].type` other than `no-control` -- whose `ref` does not resolve to a path in this tree.** The rule is written down, the control is named, and the control is not there.

The term used to cover a second sense too: a rule missing an owner, a disposition or a review-by date. That sense is real and it is enforced -- by `required` below and by `disposition.controls`'s `minItems` -- but it is NOT called orphaning, because a term meaning two things lets the cheap half be closed while the expensive half is reported as done, which is the inheritance ADR-053 refused to hand M07. Missing fields are refused by this schema; orphaning is refused by `pave/rules.py::orphan_rules`, which JSON Schema cannot express because it cannot resolve a path. The schema carries the definition, the check carries the enforcement, and they say the same sentence (ADR-075 amendment 2).

effective.description: Mandatory from M09 (ADR-053's owe, ADR-075 amendment 2): the date the source becomes binding. Required rather than optional so that a rule cannot switch off its own review clock by omitting the field it is checked against.

scope.description: What the rule reaches, in the terms of the system it is enforced against — and what it does NOT, with what would bring an excluded sense back. **A rule re-scoped by its owning seat says so here rather than by a quiet edit to `title`.** M09 met the need at MER-AI-0001: the rule was written for AI-generated *recaps*, was disposed against a service that produces no recappable content — `data/catalog.json` carries no outcome field for any title, and `grounded-017` requires the agent NOT to narrate a result — so a recap-shaped control could only ever have failed for a reason that was not the control. Re-scoping the rule to the editorial copy the bound service actually authors is a Legal/S&P decision; recording it as a field is what stops the next reader taking `title` for the whole of it (ADR-075 amendment 2 §6).

excludes.description: A sense the rule no longer reaches, named rather than deleted. A scope narrowed by silence cannot be audited

revives.description: What would bring the excluded sense back into force. Never blank: an exclusion with no revival condition is a retirement wearing a narrower name

limits.description: What this disposition does NOT cover, each owed to a seat and dated. **A disposition records its own boundary, or the registry reports a rule discharged that is only partly discharged.** M09 met this at MER-AI-0001: an L3 eval pack asserts the disclosure field on an ANSWER, and the publish-class action that puts editorial copy in front of viewers carries a separate `ai_generated` flag that can be defaulted false with every semantic check green. `pave rules trace` prints these beside the controls, so a reader of the registry lookup sees the boundary at the same moment as the chain (ADR-075 amendment 2; Tool Owner seat, M09 PR 2 round 1).

limit.description: What the disposition does not reach, in the terms the rule uses

dated.description: The milestone or trigger that closes it. Never blank: an undated limit is a residual nobody inherits

controls.description: At least one enforcing control, or an explicit reasoned 'no-control' record. Every `ref` on a control whose `type` is not `no-control` must resolve to a path in this tree; one that does not is an ORPHAN RULE, in this file's one sense of that term (see the top-level description). JSON Schema cannot check it, so `pave/rules.py::orphan_rules` does.
